THE OBITUARY, TRANSCRIBED IN FULL (OCR, line breaks as printed in the column;
the accents and the "Collége" for "Collège" are the OCR's, not the magazine's)

IN MEMORIAM

ROSS SEAMAN
1921-1987

ONCORDIA UNIVERSITY, THE YMCA, and Dawson College lost a community leader,
education innovator, and consummate teacher with the passing October 23 of
A. Ross Seaman at age 66.

At the time of his death, he was in his third year as a full-time Concordia
faculty member in Leisure Studies, where he served as Acting Chair in 1986-87.
He came to Concordia after retiring from Dawson College, where he developed the
very successful program in Community Recreation Leadership Training.

While at Concordia, Ross and his wife Margaret played central roles in the
development of Elderhostel on Loyola campus, acting as host and hostess of the
program over the past three summers.

Ross's history at Concordia goes back to the 1940s when he attended Sir George
as a YMCA Fellowship Secretary.

His first career was with the YMCA, where his contribution focused on community
work and camping. He was director of Camp Kanawana for many years, and a primary
organizer of the Quebec Camping Association and founder of the wilderness
program Les Voyageurs de la Verendrye. During this period, he introduced camping
courses to the Sir George curriculum.

Ross had been a part-time faculty member in Applied Social Science since the
department was formed in 1963, and was also active in the program and research
of the Centre for Human Relations and Community Studies.

As a consultant, he played a major role in the development of techniques of
specialized education, active retirement, and volunteer training at Collége
Marie-Victorin.

THE A. ROSS SEAMAN LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT FUND

Representatives from Concordia, Dawson College, the YMCA and Camp Kanawana met
on November 10 to set up a fund to provide scholarships for students in
leadership development programs. Inquiries or cheques should be directed to:

The A. Ross Seaman Leadership Development Fund,
Concordia University,
Financial Aid Office,
Loyola Campus, AD-130-4,
7141 Sherbrooke St. West,
Montreal, Quebec
H4B 1R6

28 CONCORDIA UNIVERSITY MAGAZINE - JANUARY 1988

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WHAT IS NEW HERE, CHECKED AGAINST wiki/people/a-ross-seaman.md BEFORE WRITING
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. BIRTH YEAR. The headline reads "ROSS SEAMAN 1921-1987" and the text says he
   died "at age 66". This answers the first half of the article's open question
   1, which read "What are Seaman's full biographical details -- birth year,
   full name, education beyond SGW?" and which a previous pass had marked
   "partly answered" because only the death date was exact. Born 1921; died
   23 October 1987 aged 66. The two are consistent only if his birthday fell on
   or before 23 October, which is a constraint on any later record, not a
   finding in itself.

2. THE DEATH DATE IS INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED. The wiki had 23 October 1987 from
   one source, the fund notice in Canadian Camping Magazine (Winter 1988). This
   is a second, separately produced document giving the same date.

3. "IN HIS THIRD YEAR AS A FULL-TIME CONCORDIA FACULTY MEMBER IN LEISURE
   STUDIES." The wiki knew only the acting chairmanship of 1986-87. Third year
   at October 1987 puts the start of the full-time appointment in 1985, which
   sits correctly against the Dawson chairmanship the wiki dates 1974-1984.

4. ELDERHOSTEL, "OVER THE PAST THREE SUMMERS." The wiki placed the Seamans'
   Elderhostel work in the 1986-87 academic year. From a January 1988 issue,
   three summers back is 1985, 1986 and 1987 -- two summers earlier than the
   wiki had it, and it was Ross and Margaret together as host and hostess.

5. "THE 1940s WHEN HE ATTENDED SIR GEORGE AS A YMCA FELLOWSHIP SECRETARY."
   Entirely new. The wiki called him "a Sir George Williams University
   graduate" with no date and no account of how he came to be there. A
   Fellowship Secretary was a YMCA staff post; the sentence says he was
   employed by the Association and studying at the same time, which makes the
   YMCA the earlier of the two attachments and Sir George an extension of it.

6. "A PRIMARY ORGANIZER OF THE QUEBEC CAMPING ASSOCIATION." A second source for
   an attribution the wiki has been careful about. The article records that the
   Montreal YMCA's press release of 28 November 1969 called Seaman "ancien
   President de l'Association des Campeurs du Quebec" and expressly does not
   adopt it, the masthead evidence showing him as Secretary rather than
   President. This obituary says "organizer", not "president" -- which is not
   the contested claim, and is compatible with the secretaryship. It should be
   used to support founding involvement, not to reopen the presidency.

7. "FOUNDER OF THE WILDERNESS PROGRAM LES VOYAGEURS DE LA VERENDRYE." The wiki
   credits Seaman's directorship with the launch of the La Verendrye canoe trip
   program and quotes a Y release naming "Les Voyageurs" as a site. This gives
   the programme's full name in one phrase and names Seaman its founder.

8. "HE INTRODUCED CAMPING COURSES TO THE SIR GEORGE CURRICULUM." New, and it
   belongs as much to wiki/connections/institutional-lineage/
   sgw-concordia-connection.md as to the biography: it is a specific channel by
   which camp practice entered a university curriculum.

9. "SINCE THE DEPARTMENT WAS FORMED IN 1963." The wiki dates Seaman's part-time
   Applied Social Science appointment to 1963 already. What is new is the
   clause: 1963 is the year the department itself was formed, which is a second
   source for the founding date that the Georgian sweep touched from the other
   side when it found H. G. Dimock in an association post in February 1962, the
   year before he founded the department.

10. COLLEGE MARIE-VICTORIN. New. Consulting on specialized education, active
    retirement and volunteer training. "Active retirement" is the same interest
    as Elderhostel, in a second institution.

11. THE FUND MEETING IS DATED AND ITS PARTIES NAMED. The wiki has the Canadian
    Camping notice saying "a group of family, friends, and colleagues met in
    early November". This says representatives of Concordia, Dawson College,
    the YMCA and Camp Kanawana met on 10 November. Same meeting, near
    certainly; this gives the day and says the four institutions sent people.
    Camp Kanawana sending a representative to a Montreal meeting three weeks
    after his death, twenty years after his directorship ended, is the fact
    worth keeping.

NULL RESULTS IN THIS ITEM. "Kanawana" occurs twice in the whole 107,758-character
issue, both on page 28, both inside this obituary. "Vankleek" does not occur;
neither does "Otoreke", "Weredale" or "Perrot". The magazine carries no other
camp material in this issue.
